title: The Paper Company That Became Dangote's Obajana Cement Works
conflicts: Import dependence: Dangote (ThisDay 2021) said 'almost 90 per cent' of cement was imported; the cement makers' association (Vanguard 2009) said local plants supplied 25.5% in 2002. Both given with attribution. Cost: $798m (IFC) and about $800m (EIB) against a $1.2bn CemNet figure seen only in snippets (site behind a bot challenge); the lenders' figure used. Capacity: 4.4 Mta planned (IFC, EIB) against 5 Mta commissioned (company); company figure used for the plant as opened. Dates: implementation from 2003 (IFC) or construction from 2004 (company), commissioning expected 2005 (IFC) and done 2007 (company); OBG's '2003 commissioning' rejected. IFC's 'first venture into cement production' conflicts with the 2000 Benue Cement purchase, so 'first' is avoided. The Kogi State claim of no payment is reported as the state's claim alongside the company's response.
notes: approx_date is 2002 (the takeover and policy year), with commissioning in 2007; the slate gave 2007. The edition includes the 2022 Kogi State dispute over the original transfer.
